audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart contradicts its own explanations on five of seven rows. whys[2] calls level 3 'your first real edge' while the chart says Shen; whys[5] says the first-item window is 'clearly yours' while the chart says Shen; whys[3] and whys[4] both say 'even'/'coin-flip' while the chart hands rows 3 and 4 to Shen and Irelia respectively; whys[0] says 'you both just farm' while row 0 says Irelia.
audit.why: Irelia is at 51.15% over 653 games here and the packet chart reads Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Skill, Skill, Irelia, Shen — which is exactly what the whys describe. The full and content layers currently agree with each other but both disagree with the prose and the data.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 rewritten as one atomic group to match the packet and the whys: Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Skill, Skill, Irelia; row 6 stays Shen. Ratings moved with them. Every phases[N].side is paired with its win[N].

audit.why: The spike set is right: level 3 for Flawless Duet, level 6 for Vanguard's Edge, first item, and Shen's late-game scaling. Shadow Dash on 18/16/14/12/10s and Stand United on 200/180/160s are the timers that gate them, and the level-6 spike now names the R interaction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states that Stand United (R) is a channel that Flawless Duet's stun cancels outright, and it never states that Ki Barrier (P) shields Shen after every spell cast. It also implies Spirit's Refuge shuts Irelia down generally, when it only blocks attacks.
audit.why: Shen R text: 'shields target allied champion... and soon after teleports' — flagged channel, interruptible. Shen W text: 'Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked' — attacks only, so Bladesurge's strike aside, Flawless Duet and Vanguard's Edge pass through it. Shen P: a shield on every spell cast, which eats the front of Irelia's burst.
audit.corrected: The R-cancel written into phases[4].why, spikes[1].text and late; the Ki Barrier shield written into dosFull[2].d; the attacks-only limit of Spirit's Refuge written into dontsFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[0].d were both boilerplate that restated the trading line instead of naming a mechanic.
audit.why: Both slots sit next to a real, checkable interaction (the passive shield and the attack-block zone) that was going unsaid.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the two mechanics above, in the same character space.

edits.before: Vanguard’s Edge walls off his disengage and marks the kill. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Shen's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Stand United is a channel — a Flawless Duet stun cancels it outright, so hold your E for his teleport as much as for his Shadow Dash.

edits.before: Vanguard's Edge walls off his Shadow Dash escape and pins him for a full all-in; if his Stand United is on cooldown he has no out.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge walls off his Shadow Dash escape and pins him for a full all-in, and Flawless Duet's stun cancels a Stand United channel outright.

edits.before: Shen wastes Shadow Dash (Taunt) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Ki Barrier shields him each spell cast — commit after he spends one.

edits.before: That is Shen's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Spirit's Refuge blocks attacks in its zone, not your E or R — poke through it.

edits.before: Shen out-stalls you the longer the game goes — his resists climb, Spirit's Refuge can blank your autos in a fight, and Stand United lets him impact skirmishes across the map you can't touch. Your duel still trades roughly even, but a 1v1 win means less when he's saving a carry top-side with his ultimate. Convert your mid-game tempo into towers and objectives early, and don't get baited into a long sidelane stand-off where his scaling and global presence quietly win the game around you.
edits.after: Shen out-stalls you the longer the game goes — his resists climb, Spirit's Refuge blanks your autos in a fight, and Stand United swings skirmishes across the map. But his ultimate is a channel: a Flawless Duet stun on him cancels the teleport outright, so hold E when you see the shield go out on a diving teammate. Convert your mid-game tempo into towers and objectives early, and don't get baited into a long sidelane stand-off where his scaling and global presence quietly win the game around you.
